messages:
leigh: heads-up: noticed reproducible degradation on long-token jobs when FP8/INT8/4bit slices are co-packed. short thread to pick low-risk next steps.
tariq: what signal are we using? degscore, user complaints?
leigh: degscore + tail_rejection_rate. reproducer shows tail_error jump from 0.03 -> 0.14 when mixed-bit batches hit.
mina: any logs/snippet?
leigh: ```
SCHED id=0xdead bits=[fp8,4bit,fp8] seq=1900 kv_hit=0.58 tail_err=0.14
SCHED id=0xbeef bits=[fp8,fp8,fp8] seq=320 kv_hit=0.93 tail_err=0.01
```
kevin: quick hypotheses: (1) kv-entry size variance causes compaction/eviction thrash, (2) implicit cross-quant reuse corrupts cached tensors if we assume fixed layout.
tariq: low-risk mitigation: add 1-byte quant_id header to KV entries so deserialization is guarded. Also add per-page "homogeneous" bit to skip compaction when mixed writes detected.
mina: header is minimal risk. homogeneity flag reduces compaction on mixed pages but may increase fragmentation. we should quantify mem increase.
kevin: scheduler-level idea: affinity buckets. If rolling tail_err for a tenant > 0.05, prefer same-bit batches for that tenant for 10 minutes (hysteresis). fallback to opportunistic packing for low-error tenants.
leigh: sounds good. telemetry needs updating: add fields: "bits_seq", "kv_hdr_present", "page_homogeneous", "tail_err", "kv_eviction_cause", "tenant_bucket". keep events cheap.
tariq: plan: (A) implement KV header + microbench (leigh+kevin), (B) implement scheduler hysteresis + bounded bucket-state (mina), (C) ops run 5% header shadow then 10% header+hysteresis canary. canary-bot: scheduled canary (5%) at 6387654340 reporting to #eng-ml-canaries.
mina: replayability: capture compact tuple (model_sha, prompt_fingerprint, seed, initial_kv_digest, bits_seq). run 0.5% shadow replays to validate before canary.
kevin: action items noted. i'll prototype header serialization (5-byte header: magic/version/quant_id/len_hi/len_lo).
leigh: i'll open tracking issue and PRs after microbench. thanks all :thumbsup:
